title: Wegovy Pricing & Coverage in Canada
summary: Wegovy coverage in Canada varies by private plan. Provincial options are limited. Phoenix provides receipts for eligible reimbursement claims. - Aug 26, 2026
body_markdown:
A lot of people assume their benefits plan will cover Wegovy the same way it covers other prescriptions. That assumption leads to some pretty uncomfortable moments at the pharmacy. The reality is that coverage for weight management GLP-1s in Canada is still patchy, but there are a few ways to bring the cost down once you know what you're working with.


**TLDR:**


- As of mid-2026, no provincial drug plan in Canada covers Wegovy for weight management, and this can change as new pricing agreements are reached.
- Negotiations between the pan-Canadian Pharmaceutical Alliance and Novo Nordisk ended without a deal in December 2025, so the coverage gap is likely to persist.
- Only about 31% of Canadian employer plans include coverage for this treatment category at all, and most of those limit coverage to other approved medical uses.
- If your private plan does cover it, expect prior authorization with approval timelines of 5 to 10 business days.
- A prescription requires assessment by a licensed healthcare provider; telehealth consultations with licensed Canadian providers are a viable path if you lack a family doctor.


## Wegovy Cost in Canada


Out-of-pocket cost for Wegovy in Canada can vary by pharmacy, province, dispensing fees, and whether any part of the cost is reimbursed through a benefits plan. Through Canadian online health clinics, Wegovy is commonly priced at approximately $399.99 per month for a full monthly supply at the highest maintenance dose, though your actual cost may be lower during earlier titration months. Online clinics typically do not bill insurers directly, but they can provide documentation you submit yourself for potential reimbursement through your group benefits plan or Health Spending Account (HSA). If a reimbursement claim is approved, you recover part of the cost after the fact; you still pay out of pocket at the time of purchase. That distinction matters when you are weighing whether your budget can absorb the upfront expense while a plan's authorization decision is pending.


Beyond Wegovy specifically, the Canadian market for this treatment category has also expanded to include a[generic version of semaglutide](https://www.phoenix.ca/medications/generic-semaglutide) , which some patients discuss with their provider as part of a broader look at available options. Manufacturers of brand-name medications in this category, including Novo Nordisk, may also offer their own patient support programs that some patients could be eligible for, with eligibility and details set directly by the manufacturer and separate from any coverage through a benefits plan or provincial program. A licensed healthcare provider can help you understand which option fits your health profile and circumstances.


## Is Wegovy Covered by Provincial Drug Plans in Canada?


Provincial drug plans across Canada currently do not extend coverage to GLP-1 medications like Wegovy for weight management. Plans such as Ontario's ODB, BC PharmaCare, and Alberta Blue Cross are commonly reported to follow this approach as of publication, though specifics can vary and change. If your prescription is written for weight loss, the public plan will not cover the cost in most provinces today, though coverage rules can change, so it is worth confirming directly with your provincial plan.


This gap traces back to a[Canadian Drug Agency recommendation](https://www.cda-amc.ca/semaglutide-1) that a price reduction be secured before public coverage for weight management could move forward. That recommendation led to negotiations between the pan-Canadian Pharmaceutical Alliance and manufacturer Novo Nordisk, which ended without an agreement in December 2025; as of mid-2026, no new deal has been announced. Until a new deal or recommendation changes the calculation, the coverage gap for weight loss use is likely to persist, according to the[Canadian Medical Association](https://www.cma.ca/healthcare-for-real/can-you-get-glp-1-drugs-canada) .


## How Private Benefits Plans Approach Wegovy Coverage in Canada


Private group benefits plans approach Wegovy coverage differently than provincial plans, though coverage still varies widely by employer and policy. About 31% of Canadian employer plans include some coverage for this treatment category. Of those plans,[56%](https://www.benefitscanada.com/benefits/health-benefits/canadian-employers-expanding-glp-1-coverage-for-weight-loss-survey/) limit that coverage to other approved medical uses, leaving only a portion of Canadian workers with a benefits plan that could apply to Wegovy for weight management.


If your plan covers it, expect paperwork before payment. Many private insurers, including Manulife, Sun Life, Canada Life, and Blue Cross, may require prior authorization in these cases, meaning your doctor would submit documentation showing medical necessity before the plan agrees to pay, though exact requirements vary by insurer and policy.


That documentation usually includes your body mass index, related health conditions, and notes on other weight management approaches you have already tried. Approval timelines run[5 to 10 business days](https://www.benefitscanada.com/benefits/health-benefits/canadian-employers-expanding-glp-1-coverage-for-weight-loss-survey/) in most cases, so plan ahead and avoid waiting until the week you want to start treatment.

## What to Ask Your Benefits Provider Before Filling Your Prescription


Before you fill anything, get answers straight from your benefits provider. A quick call or portal check can save you from a pharmacy counter surprise. Here is what to ask:


- Is this treatment listed on my plan's formulary, and what conditions or uses does that coverage apply to?
- Does my plan require prior authorization, and if so, what form does my provider need to submit?
- What clinical documentation does my licensed healthcare provider need to include, such as body mass index or related health conditions?
- Is there a step therapy requirement, meaning I need to try and fail other treatments first?
- Are there annual or lifetime maximums on coverage, and how much of that maximum would this prescription use up?
- How long does approval typically take, and is there an expedited option if timing matters?


Write down the answers and the name of the person you spoke with. Benefits departments handle a high volume of calls, and a paper trail matters if your claim gets denied or delayed later.

The consultation fee for a first online assessment is typically waived for new patients. While men's online health clinics do not bill your benefits plan directly, they provide the prescription documentation and receipts you need to submit a reimbursement claim yourself, so if your employer plan covers any portion of the treatment cost, you may be able to recover it after the fact, subject to your plan's terms. For any out-of-pocket amount you pay, eligible prescription costs may also qualify for the Medical Expense Tax Credit, which can partially offset what you spend over the course of a year. A licensed healthcare provider can help you understand which treatment approach fits your health profile and circumstances.


## How the Medical Expense Tax Credit Applies to Wegovy Costs


The Medical Expense Tax Credit (METC) is a non-refundable federal tax credit that lets you offset a portion of eligible out-of-pocket healthcare costs, and prescription medications obtained through a licensed Canadian healthcare provider generally qualify. What you pay out of pocket for a prescribed weight management treatment may be eligible for your METC claim in the tax year you paid it, subject to CRA rules. The credit applies to eligible medical expenses that exceed a threshold set by the CRA, typically a percentage of your net income or a fixed annual floor, whichever is lower. Review the CRA's current guidelines or speak with a tax professional to confirm the exact figures and your eligibility for the relevant tax year. Keep every receipt from your pharmacy or online health clinic, since the CRA requires documentation showing the amount paid and confirmation that the expense was for a prescribed treatment. If you are also submitting a reimbursement claim through your employer benefits plan or Health Spending Account, only the unreimbursed portion may be eligible for the METC, since costs your plan already covered generally cannot be claimed again. This section is educational only and is not individual tax advice; consult the CRA or a qualified tax professional for guidance specific to your situation.


## How to Get a[Wegovy Prescription](https://www.phoenix.ca/medications/wegovy) in Canada


Getting a prescription in Canada starts with a licensed healthcare provider, whether that is a family doctor, a weight management clinic, or a licensed online provider. No legitimate source provides treatment without one, and any site or seller claiming otherwise should raise a red flag.


The clinical assessment looks similar across each path. Your provider reviews your body mass index, medical history, and any conditions that might affect eligibility, such as thyroid issues or a history of pancreatitis. They also ask about other weight management approaches you have already tried, since this often factors into whether treatment makes sense for you.


Telehealth has changed who can access this process. If you lack a family doctor, or prefer to skip an in-person visit, a text-based consultation with a licensed Canadian provider covers the same ground, minus the waiting room.

Men's online health clinics are one of the most practical starting points for anyone trying to access GLP-1 weight management treatment in Canada, particularly if you do not have a family doctor, a situation that applies to[more than 6.5 million Canadians](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10125184/) . The process starts with a confidential online health assessment that a licensed Canadian healthcare provider reviews to determine whether treatment is clinically appropriate for you; no in-person appointment or referral is required. Because these clinics do not bill insurers directly, you pay out of pocket at the time of purchase, but they provide the prescription documentation and receipts you need to submit a reimbursement claim through your employer benefits plan or Health Spending Account after the fact. Ongoing support through your provider also means that as your weight management plan evolves, adjustments to your treatment can happen without scheduling a new appointment.


## Final Thoughts on Wegovy Coverage in Canada


Coverage for weight management treatment in Canada varies by plan, and many patients still pay some or all of the cost out of pocket. Reviewing your benefits plan details, starting the prior authorization process early if your plan requires it, and working with a licensed healthcare provider on any needed documentation can help you plan ahead. Coverage rules can also change, so confirming current details directly with your provincial plan or benefits provider is worth the extra step.


## FAQ


### How much does Wegovy cost per month with insurance in Canada?


The cost of Wegovy with insurance coverage in Canada varies depending on your plan, but most private benefits plans that cover it for weight management still require prior authorization and may apply annual or lifetime maximums. Without coverage, Wegovy runs approximately $399.99 per month at Canadian online health clinics. Checking your plan's formulary and confirming whether coverage applies to weight management is the most reliable way to know your actual out-of-pocket cost, since coverage details can vary and change.


### Does insurance cover Wegovy for weight loss in Canada?


Coverage depends entirely on your individual private benefits plan, so checking your plan's formulary directly is the most reliable way to know. Some Canadian private plans limit coverage for this treatment category to other approved medical uses, which means your out-of-pocket cost for weight management use may still be the full retail price. Provincial drug plans such as Ontario's ODB and BC PharmaCare do not list Wegovy for weight management as of this writing, though coverage rules can change, so it's worth confirming current details with your provincial plan.


### What is the average cost of Wegovy with insurance, and what affects what you actually pay?


The average cost of Wegovy with insurance depends on three factors: whether your plan's formulary includes it for weight loss, whether prior authorization is approved, and whether your plan has a drug maximum that limits how much it will pay out annually. Your licensed healthcare provider will typically need to submit documentation covering your BMI, related health conditions, and previous weight management attempts before approval. That review process runs 5 to 10 business days at most insurers.


### Can I get a Wegovy prescription in Canada without seeing a doctor in person?


Yes. A text-based consultation with a licensed Canadian healthcare provider covers the same clinical ground as an in-person visit, including a review of your BMI, medical history, and eligibility factors like thyroid conditions or a history of pancreatitis, without a waiting room or travel. This path is particularly useful if you do not have a family doctor. No prescription is guaranteed; the provider makes an independent clinical decision based on your health profile.
